SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In which part do you find the seeds of a mango? (1 mark)
   A. Stem
   B. Root
   C. Leaf
   D. Fruit

2. What happens to a dead plant? (1 mark)
   A. It turns into an animal
   B. It becomes a rock
   C. It flies away
   D. It rots and returns nutrients to the soil

3. What does removing waste mean for a plant? (1 mark)
   A. Sending out roots
   B. Throwing away its seeds
   C. Cutting its own leaves
   D. Getting rid of things its body does not need

4. Which part of a bean plant grows in the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Pods
   B. Leaves
   C. Flowers
   D. Roots

5. Maize lives for one season and then dies. A baobab lives for many years. What does this show? (1 mark)
   A. Only maize is alive
   B. Baobab does not die
   C. Maize never grows
   D. Plants live for different lengths of time

6. Which of these shows a plant reproducing? (1 mark)
   A. A leaf turning green
   B. A stem getting taller
   C. A root drinking water
   D. A bean plant making pods with seeds

7. Which part of the plant holds it firmly in the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Leaves
   B. Fruit
   C. Roots
   D. Flowers

8. Which of these animals is an amphibian? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Toad
   C. Snake
   D. Tortoise

9. A caterpillar changes into a butterfly. Which sign of life does this best show? (1 mark)
   A. Breathing out
   B. Dying
   C. Growing
   D. Feeding only

10. Frogs have smooth, wet skin and spend part of their life in water. They are (1 mark)
   A. Birds
   B. Reptiles
   C. Amphibians
   D. Mammals

11. A pupil finds a small animal under a stone. It has a long soft body, no legs and no shell. It is probably (1 mark)
   A. A frog
   B. An earthworm
   C. A lizard
   D. A snake

12. Where does the digestive tube begin? (1 mark)
   A. Small intestine
   B. Stomach
   C. Mouth
   D. Anus

13. Which of these do we drink to keep digestion healthy? (1 mark)
   A. Sugary drinks all the time
   B. Clean safe water
   C. Muddy water
   D. Nothing

14. What is digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Storing food in the stomach for years
   B. Throwing away food
   C. Making food hot
   D. Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use

15. Why should you wear shoes and wash hands to prevent worms? (1 mark)
   A. Worms live in shoes
   B. Worm eggs are found in dirty soil and on dirty hands
   C. Shoes make food digest
   D. Water makes worms grow

16. What is constipation? (1 mark)
   A. Vomiting
   B. Having worms
   C. Passing watery faeces
   D. Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty

17. How many grams are in 5 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 50
   B. 5000
   C. 50 000
   D. 500

18. Which of these is a liquid used as fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Air
   B. Charcoal
   C. Firewood
   D. Paraffin

19. An empty bottle is full of (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Air
   C. Nothing
   D. Sand

20. What does recycle mean? (1 mark)
   A. Make waste into new things
   B. Burn waste
   C. Throw waste away
   D. Bury waste

21. Which living things help waste to decompose? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic bags
   B. Stones
   C. Fungi and bacteria
   D. Bottles

22. Which is an example of reducing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing a bottle in a river
   B. Leaving litter at a picnic
   C. Carrying a cloth shopping bag
   D. Burning plastic

23. Which of these makes a good compost mixture? (1 mark)
   A. Glass and metal
   B. Plastic and tins
   C. Vegetable peelings, dry leaves and some soil
   D. Batteries and plastic

24. What is a good message for a water conservation poster? (1 mark)
   A. Water is free for all to waste
   B. Close the tap after use
   C. Waste is fun
   D. Leave the tap open

25. Which of these is a source of dirty water we should not drink? (1 mark)
   A. Safe borehole water
   B. Clean tap water
   C. Boiled and treated water
   D. Water used to wash clothes

26. A flat sheet of paper falls slower than a stone because (1 mark)
   A. Paper is bigger
   B. Gravity does not pull paper
   C. Air pushes up on the flat paper more
   D. The stone is bigger

27. Which of these is NOT an effect of force? (1 mark)
   A. Stopping motion
   B. Starting motion
   C. Changing shape
   D. Making something have colour

28. What effect of force is shown when a goalkeeper stops a ball? (1 mark)
   A. Makes it lighter
   B. Changes its colour
   C. Stops a moving object
   D. Starts a moving object

29. Why do matches light when rubbed on the box? (1 mark)
   A. Friction makes cold
   B. Friction makes heat
   C. Gravity makes light
   D. Wind makes fire

30. Pulling a rope in tug of war uses (1 mark)
   A. Only gravity
   B. Only heat
   C. A pull force
   D. Only light

31. Which of these needs friction to work? (1 mark)
   A. Sliding on oil
   B. Walking on the ground
   C. A rolling wheel
   D. Skating on wet ice

32. Which of these shows that friction produces heat? (1 mark)
   A. Pouring water
   B. Looking at a torch
   C. Rubbing hands together
   D. Drawing with chalk

33. Which of these is a push? (1 mark)
   A. Opening a drawer by its handle
   B. Kicking a football
   C. Pulling a cart
   D. Drawing water with a rope

34. Which of these is transparent? (1 mark)
   A. Metal
   B. Clear glass
   C. Thick cardboard
   D. Wood

35. A lighthouse is used to (1 mark)
   A. Grow plants
   B. Dry clothes
   C. Warn ships of danger
   D. Cook food

36. How does light travel? (1 mark)
   A. In zigzags
   B. In circles
   C. In straight lines
   D. In curves only

37. Which of these uses sunlight to dry things? (1 mark)
   A. Making rain only
   B. Making stones
   C. Making ice
   D. Drying clothes and grain

38. Why do houses have windows? (1 mark)
   A. To keep out light
   B. To make noise
   C. To let in daylight
   D. To let in only rain

39. What is a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. Something that reflects light
   B. Something that gives out its own light
   C. Something that is dark
   D. Something that blocks light

40. What should you do first if you burn your skin? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Put it under cool running water and tell an adult
   C. Put butter on it
   D. Cover it with soil

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name the part of a plant that makes food and the part that makes seeds. (2 marks)

42. Explain the dangers of solid waste to health, animals and the environment. (5 marks)

43. Describe the differences between mammals and birds. (4 marks)

44. Describe how a bean seed grows into a young plant. (3 marks)

45. Explain how animals show the signs of life: feeding, growing, and reproducing. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

46. Describe an activity that shows the uses of heat, for example drying clothes in different conditions. (5 marks)

47. Why do we use kitchen gloves when holding hot pots? (2 marks)

48. Describe how you can show that rough surfaces give more friction than smooth ones. (3 marks)

49. Explain why a translucent roof sheet is useful in a classroom during the day. (3 marks)

50. Why is used washing water not safe for drinking? Give one good way to use it. (3 marks)

51. Give three problems caused by friction. (3 marks)

52. Give two symptoms of an unhealthy digestive system. (2 marks)

53. State three ways of keeping teeth healthy. (3 marks)

54. Describe the journey of a mouthful of food from the mouth to the anus. (4 marks)

55. Give three safety rules when using sources of light. (3 marks)

56. Describe how to investigate the effect of different surfaces on friction using a ramp and a block. Include what you keep the same. (5 marks)

57. Why is the moon not a source of light? (2 marks)

58. Name two things a farmer can do to save water. (2 marks)

59. State two jobs of the mouth in digestion. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Fruit
   Seeds are found inside fruits.

2. D — It rots and returns nutrients to the soil
   Dead plants decay and give nutrients back to the soil.

3. D — Getting rid of things its body does not need
   Living things must remove waste made in their bodies.

4. D — Roots
   Roots grow underground.

5. D — Plants live for different lengths of time
   All plants die, but some live for one season and others for many years.

6. D — A bean plant making pods with seeds
   Making seeds is reproduction. Growing taller is growth.

7. C — Roots
   Roots anchor the plant in the ground.

8. B — Toad
   Toads have moist skin and start life in water.

9. C — Growing
   A caterpillar grows and changes form to become a butterfly.

10. C — Amphibians
   These features describe amphibians.

11. B — An earthworm
   An earthworm is a soft, legless invertebrate.

12. C — Mouth
   Food enters the body through the mouth.

13. B — Clean safe water
   Clean safe water helps digestion and prevents disease.

14. D — Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use
   Digestion breaks food into tiny parts that can pass into the blood.

15. B — Worm eggs are found in dirty soil and on dirty hands
   Worm eggs can enter the body through dirt.

16. D — Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty
   Constipation means hard faeces that are difficult to pass.

17. B — 5000
   5 x 1000 = 5000 g.

18. D — Paraffin
   Paraffin and petrol are liquid fuels.

19. B — Air
   An empty bottle contains air.

20. A — Make waste into new things
   Recycling makes new things from old materials.

21. C — Fungi and bacteria
   Decomposers such as fungi and bacteria break down waste.

22. C — Carrying a cloth shopping bag
   A reusable bag means fewer plastic bags are thrown away.

23. C — Vegetable peelings, dry leaves and some soil
   Composting uses natural plant waste.

24. B — Close the tap after use
   A short, clear message helps people remember.

25. D — Water used to wash clothes
   Used washing water is dirty and unsafe.

26. C — Air pushes up on the flat paper more
   Air pushes up more on the wide flat sheet.

27. D — Making something have colour
   Colour is not caused by a force.

28. C — Stops a moving object
   The force of the hands stops the ball.

29. B — Friction makes heat
   Rubbing produces heat.

30. C — A pull force
   Pulling is a force.

31. B — Walking on the ground
   Walking needs grip from friction.

32. C — Rubbing hands together
   Rubbing surfaces produces heat.

33. B — Kicking a football
   A kick pushes the ball.

34. B — Clear glass
   Clear glass lets light through.

35. C — Warn ships of danger
   Lighthouses show ships where land or rocks are.

36. C — In straight lines
   Light travels in straight lines.

37. D — Drying clothes and grain
   Sunlight dries wet things.

38. C — To let in daylight
   Windows allow sunlight to enter the room.

39. B — Something that gives out its own light
   A source of light makes its own light.

40. B — Put it under cool running water and tell an adult
   Cool water reduces the burn.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Leaves make food and flowers (fruits) make seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Health: flies and rats spread diseases, mosquitoes breed in tins. Animals: goats eat polythene and die. Environment: blocked drains, polluted water, harmful smoke from burning.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for health, 1 mark for animals and 2 marks for environment.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mammals have hair or fur and feed their young on milk and most give birth to live young. Birds have feathers and wings and lay eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four differences.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: The seed takes in water and a root comes out first and goes down. Then a shoot grows up and opens into leaves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for water and seed, 1 mark for root first, 1 mark for shoot and leaves.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Feeding: a goat eats grass. Growing: a chick becomes a hen. Reproducing: a hen lays eggs, or a cow gives birth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign with example, plus 1 mark for explaining growth as getting bigger.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wet two similar cloths. Hang one in the sun and the other in the shade. After some time, feel them. The cloth in the sun dries faster because heat from the sun evaporates the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for fair comparison, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gloves are poor passers of heat so they protect hands from burns.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for poor at passing heat and 1 mark for protection from burns.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Slide the same block down a ramp covered with different surfaces. It travels a shorter distance on rough surfaces than on smooth ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: It lets daylight in, so lamps are not needed, saving electricity and money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for daylight, 1 mark for no lamps, 1 mark for saving.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has dirt and germs. It can be used to water plants or mop floors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirty water, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for a safe use.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: It wears away shoes and tyres, wastes energy, makes machines hot and slows moving parts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation, worms (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Brush at least twice a day, limit sweets and sugary drinks, visit a dentist, use clean toothbrush or chewing stick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Chewed in the mouth, swallowed, pushed down the gullet, churned in the stomach, digested and absorbed in the small intestine, water taken back in the large intestine, faeces stored in the rectum and passed out of the anus.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for every two correct steps up to 4.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Never look directly at the sun, do not shine torches in eyes, keep candles and lamps away from curtains and paper, do not touch hot bulbs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a ramp. Slide a block down it covered with cloth, paper, cardboard and bare board. Measure how far it slides each time. Keep the same block, same ramp height and same push. Record in a table. The shortest distance shows the most friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for ramp, 1 mark for surfaces, 1 mark for measuring, 1 mark for fair test, 1 mark for conclusion.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: It does not make its own light. It reflects light from the sun.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for no light of its own and 1 mark for reflecting sunlight.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Use drip irrigation, use mulch, water at cooler times, harvest rainwater.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Teeth cut and grind food. The tongue moves food and saliva wets it and starts digesting starch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct job.
